<!--block:B0011-->
Finite-cover products can agree on a selected stratum or finite panel
without recovering every primitive owner. P32 fixes this distinction at
the object level. The base is a marked closed hyperbolic genus-two
surface with unit-speed geodesic flow and presentation

\begin{verbatim}
Gamma=<a1,b1,a2,b2 | [a1,b1][a2,b2]=1>.
\end{verbatim}

<!--block:B0013-->
The cover tower is the pure homology tower
\texttt{H\_N=ker(Gamma\ -\textgreater{}\ H\_1(Sigma;Z/NZ))}. It is not
the residual inverse-limit object studied in the preceding branch, and a
conclusion about one tower cannot repair the other. Owners are oriented
primitive surface-group conjugacy classes; inverse classes remain
separately oriented. For an owner with homology vector in
\texttt{Z\^{}4}, content \texttt{d} is the greatest common divisor of
the absolute coordinates, with zero content treated as a separate case.

<!--block:B0014-->
The normalization is immutable. Physical lifted time is multiplied by
exactly \texttt{1/N}, and the logarithm of the raw lift-component
product is multiplied by exactly \texttt{1/N\^{}3}. Content-dependent
changes, outcome-dependent weights, adaptive schedules, and
favorable-panel selection are prohibited. The universal endpoint
concerns all owner contents, not an average and not the content-one
subproduct alone.

<!--block:B0015-->
The revised research question is:

<!--block:B0016-->
\textbf{Do the prospectively derived local factors for higher-content
and zero-content owners already obstruct the frozen \texttt{1/N} and
\texttt{1/N\^{}3} full-owner recovery scheme; and only if those adverse
tests are survived, what formal and analytic obligations remain for the
content-one subproduct?}

<!--block:B0017-->
The change is methodological. It does not assert that the candidate factors
are correct or that an obstruction exists. Higher- and zero-content checks are
earlier in the declared dependency graph because they require fewer named
downstream objects than formal topology and compact-uniform tails. This is not
an empirical runtime, proof-complexity, or information-gain estimate. A closed
adverse result would settle the universal endpoint negatively under the fixed
scheme; survival would license only the next predeclared obligation. A positive
content-one statement, if eventually proved, would remain restricted.

<!--block:B0019-->
The word ``owner'' is universal in this article. It never means only a
content-one class. The population comprises oriented primitive
surface-group conjugacy classes across positive higher content, content
one, and the separately typed zero-content case. Inverse classes remain
distinct. This corrects a potentially misleading shorthand in an older
state description and prevents a favorable exceptional stratum from
being substituted for the frozen all-owner endpoint.

<!--block:B0020-->
Three gates organize the program. The owner gate must bind equality,
oriented conjugacy, maximal roots, inverse handling, serialization, and
prefix completeness to the marked presentation. The local-factor gate
must derive cover order, component multiplicity, primitive-lift status,
rescaled period, and normalized exponent for each relevant content. The
formal/analytic gate must supply the coefficient objects and, if local
tests survive, the uniform tail theorem. A failure at an earlier gate
stops later work; it is not repaired by changing a schedule, selecting a
favorable panel, or moving to a different tower.

<!--block:B0021-->
The falsification-first order is therefore informational rather than
promotional. It asks the shortest exact questions capable of deciding
the universal proposal while leaving survival, obstruction, and
not-evaluable outcomes all open. The architecture does not infer a
mismatch from the displayed shapes of unproved formulas, and it does not
infer convergence from a finite diagnostic plan.

<!--block:B0053-->
For a positive-content owner \texttt{g}, let its content be
\texttt{d\textgreater{}0} and define prospectively
\texttt{q\_N(g)=gcd(N,d)}. The frozen program asks a later proof to
derive the deck order, primitive-lift count, physical lifted period, and
normalized local factor, including the target expression

<!--block:B0054-->
\begin{verbatim}
F_N,g(s)=(1-exp(-s ell(g)/q_N(g)))^(-q_N(g)).
\end{verbatim}

<!--block:B0055-->
For zero content, the frozen program treats the owner separately and
targets

<!--block:B0056-->
\begin{verbatim}
F_N,g^(0)(s)=(1-exp(-s ell(g)/N))^(-N).
\end{verbatim}

<!--block:B0057-->
Neither expression is a result of this article. A proof must derive them from
the deck action under the exact marked presentation, establish the
component count and covering degree, prove primitiveness of lifted
components, and account for both \texttt{1/N} time scaling and
\texttt{1/N\^{}3} log multiplicity. The zero-content expression cannot
be obtained by informal substitution into the positive-content case.

<!--block:B0058-->
The base primitive-owner factor used for the proposed comparison is

<!--block:B0059-->
\begin{verbatim}
B_g(s)=(1-exp(-s ell(g)))^(-1).
\end{verbatim}

<!--block:B0060-->
\begingroup\sloppy
\textbf{Conditional scalar lemma.}  If \(\ell>0\), \(s>0\) is real, and
\(m\geq2\) is an integer, then
\[
 \Phi_m(s)=\bigl(1-e^{-s\ell/m}\bigr)^{-m}
 \;>\;
 B(s)=\bigl(1-e^{-s\ell}\bigr)^{-1}.
\]
Indeed, put \(x=e^{-s\ell/m}\).  Then \(0<x<1\) and
\(e^{-s\ell}=x^m\).  Since \(m\geq2\),
\[
 (1-x)^m<(1-x)<(1-x^m).
\]
All three quantities are positive, so taking reciprocals reverses both strict
inequalities:
\[
 (1-x)^{-m}>(1-x)^{-1}>(1-x^m)^{-1}.
\]
The outer terms are \(\Phi_m(s)\) and \(B(s)\).  The proof audit is
\path{notes/stage4_prime_conditional_scalar_lemma_audit_round2.json}
(SHA-256 \texttt{41759b42\allowbreak{}a0a4b329\allowbreak{}be15541a\allowbreak{}4cdb9a4f\allowbreak{}3cf4fdb3\allowbreak{}0b80ecae\allowbreak{}a402d035\allowbreak{}51e5a9c1}).  This exact lemma concerns candidate positive real
functions only; it performs no factor derivation, owner observation, coefficient
execution, global obstruction, recovery determination, or Route evaluation.
\par\endgroup

<!--block:B0061-->
The positive-content derivation contract now exposes its intermediate
targets. For homology content \texttt{d>0} and
\texttt{q\_N(g)=gcd(N,d)}, the proposed identities are deck-image order
\texttt{N/q\_N(g)}, lifted-component count
\(N^3 q_N(g)\), scaled period \texttt{ell(g)/q\_N(g)}, and logarithmically
normalized exponent \texttt{q\_N(g)}. Chaining only those proposed fields
gives the displayed \texttt{F\_N,g}; every identity has status
\texttt{UNPROVED}. A future ledger must bind the homology vector, content, deck
action, component count, covering degree, primitive-lift proof, unscaled and
scaled periods, raw exponent, both frozen normalizations, and resulting factor.
The zero-content ledger remains separate, and a read-only verifier must reject
any unresolved field.

<!--block:B0062-->
The two normalizations must be visible at different levels. Multiplying
physical lifted time by $1/N$ changes the exponential argument, whereas
multiplying the logarithm of the raw component product by $1/N^3$
changes its exponent after component counting. Combining those
operations informally can hide a missing power or an unjustified
primitive-component assumption. The future proof must therefore derive
the raw lift product first and apply each frozen normalization in its
declared order.

<!--block:B0063-->

\subsection{First adverse target: higher
content}\label{42-first-adverse-target-higher-content}}

<!--block:B0064-->
The controlling modulus schedule is \texttt{N\_k=k!} for every integer
\texttt{k\textgreater{}=1}. For a fixed positive content
\texttt{d\textgreater{}1}, the candidate formula would eventually have
\texttt{q\_N(g)=d} whenever the factorial modulus is divisible by
\texttt{d}. The proposed local factor would then have the stabilized
displayed shape

<!--block:B0065-->
\begin{verbatim}
(1-exp(-s ell(g)/d))^(-d).
\end{verbatim}

<!--block:B0066-->
For a higher-content owner with \(d\geq2\), the lemma applies with
\(m=d\) only after the frozen factorial schedule reaches \(d\mid N\), a valid
cover calculation derives the displayed higher-content factor with
\(q_N(g)=d\), and the permitted finite scalar or singleton comparison is bound.
Under all of those antecedents it gives the strict scalar inequality
\(\Phi_d(s)>B(s)\) for every real \(s>0\).  None of the antecedent scientific
derivations or an ownerwise execution is present here.  Thus this is a conditional
implication, not a reported mismatch or global obstruction; failure of any gate
returns \texttt{NOT\_EVALUABLE}.

<!--block:B0067-->
This priority is falsification-first because it can decide the universal
endpoint before a global infinite product is built. It also prevents a
content-one success from concealing an adverse owner class.

<!--block:B0068-->
The higher-content test is ownerwise and target blind. A later execution
would have to select an eligible owner under the frozen owner interface,
not because its displayed length or content appears favorable. It would
then derive the factor and project to the independently named owner

Let \(\mathcal O_+\) and \(\mathcal O_0\) be disjoint typed sets of
oriented primitive owners with \(d(g)\geq1\) and \(d(g)=0\), respectively, and
\(\ell(g)>0\).  The positive carrier retains the frozen initial system.  For a
finite \(F\subset\mathcal O_+\) and \(D\in\mathbb N_0\), set
\[
 \mathfrak m_F=(u_g:g\in F),\qquad
 R_{F,D}=\mathbb Q[u_g:g\in F]/\mathfrak m_F^{D+1}.
\]
Order indices by \((F,D)\preceq(F',D')\) exactly when
\(F\subseteq F'\) and \(D\leq D'\).  The map
\(\rho_{(F',D'),(F,D)}:R_{F',D'}\to R_{F,D}\) sets variables in
\(F'\setminus F\) to zero and then truncates total degree above \(D\).  Define
\[
 R_+=\varprojlim_{(F,D)}R_{F,D}.
\]
Each coordinate has the discrete topology and \(R_+\) has the inverse-limit
topology.  Equality means equality in every \((F,D)\) coordinate; convergence
means eventual coordinate stability.  Thus \(R_+\) is a Hausdorff complete
topological \(\mathbb Q\)-algebra, independently of any scalar product.

Every denominator has constant term one.  Its truncated geometric inverse in

 \ S\subset\mathbb Q_{\geq0}\text{ well ordered}\right\}.
\]
Equality is rational-exponent coefficientwise and the valuation topology has
neighborhoods \(v(f)>r\), where \(v(f)=\min\operatorname{supp}f\).
The zero type is the tagged family
\(R_0=\bigsqcup_{g\in\mathcal O_0}\{g\}\times H_g\): operations occur only
inside one \(H_g\), with no cross-owner product and no coercion to \(R_+\).
For fixed \(N\), put

[(1-z_g^{1/N})^{-1},(1-z_g)^{-1}]\subset H_g\) and define
\(\tau_{s,g,N}:A^0_{g,N}\to\mathbb C\) by

literature comparison

<!--block:B0083-->
\textbf{Formal compatibility lemma.}  The transition maps above are
well-defined continuous unital homomorphisms, satisfy identity and composition,
and make \(R_+\) Hausdorff and complete.  The maps \(j_F\) are injective and
commute with finite-owner restriction.  For every \(g\in\mathcal O_+\),
\[
 \pi_g:R_+\longrightarrow
 \mathbb Q[[u_g]]=\varprojlim_D\mathbb Q[u_g]/(u_g^{D+1})
\]
is a well-defined continuous unital homomorphism satisfying
\(\pi_{g,D}=\rho_{(F,D),(\{g\},D)}\circ p_{F,D}\) for every finite
\(F\ni g\).  Hahn convolution and the stated finite scalar maps are likewise
well defined.

<!--block:B0135-->
\emph{Proof.}  Variable deletion preserves total degree; hence an element of
\(\mathfrak m_{F'}^{D'+1}\) maps to zero modulo
\(\mathfrak m_F^{D+1}\) when \(D\leq D'\).  Substitution and truncation
compose, proving the inverse-system laws.  The limit is the closed equalizer of
these laws inside a product of complete Hausdorff discrete algebras, so it is
complete and Hausdorff.  In every truncation, \((1-u_g^r)^{-1}\) is the finite
geometric sum through degree \(D\), and these sums commute with transition.  If
\(j_F(p/q)=0\), multiplying by the unit expansion of \(q\) gives \(p=0\) in
every degree, hence \(p=0\); thus \(j_F\) is injective.  The inverse-limit
equations make \(\pi_g\) independent of \(F\) and prove its displayed
compatibility.  For well-ordered supports in \(\mathbb Q_{\geq0}\), sums of
supports are well ordered and each exponent has finitely many decompositions:
an infinite family would contain increasing exponents in one support and force
a descending family in the other.  Hahn convolution is therefore
coefficient-finite; the candidate supports \(\{r/N:r\geq0\}\) and
\(\{r:r\geq0\}\) qualify.  Finally, \(\operatorname{Re}s>0\) makes every
evaluated monomial have modulus below one, so the declared denominator images
are nonzero.  The full audit is
\path{notes/stage4_prime_formal_definition_audit_round2.json} (SHA-256

elements of \(R_+\) are equal, their \(\pi_g\) images are equal; therefore a
proved inequality in one compatible singleton coordinate disproves equality of

made only inside its tagged \(H_g\) fiber.  Conversely, singleton projections
are not jointly faithful on mixed-owner monomials: for distinct \(g,h\), every
singleton projection kills \(u_gu_h\).  Thus the lemma neither constructs nor
recovers a global product.  The conditional scalar inequality can witness a
local difference only after the corresponding project factor is independently
derived and mapped through the declared finite scalar domain.  Those scientific
antecedents remain absent, so no ownerwise observation, obstruction, recovery,
or Route credit follows.

## Abstract

P32 studies a fixed renormalization proposal for the pure genus-two homology-cover tower `H_N=ker(Gamma -> H_1(Sigma;Z/NZ))`. Physical lifted time is scaled by exactly `1/N`, and the logarithm of the raw lift-component product by exactly `1/N^3`. The universal endpoint asks for recovery of every oriented primitive base-owner factor. Phase-5 review found that the earlier four-package presentation understated the adverse information already visible in its own prospective local factors. Revision 1 therefore adopts a falsification-first architecture. Conditional on a future derivation of those factors, positive content `d>1` and zero content become the first theorem targets; they must be settled before formal or compact-uniform resources are invested in the exceptional content-one stratum. The content-one analytic program is now explicitly contingent and secondary. The project-defined inverse-limit object `R_+`, its localizations and projections, and the separate zero-content Hahn object remain unresolved constructions. Likewise, any analytic tail theorem is conditional on survival of the local tests and would require an absolute logarithmic-summand majorant uniform on each frozen compact set and compatible with every specified limit order. **Keywords:** homology covers; ownerwise factors; falsification-first methods; primitive geodesics; formal products; compact-uniform convergence

## 1. Introduction, Research Question, and Contribution

Finite-cover products can agree on a selected stratum or finite panel without recovering every primitive owner. P32 fixes this distinction at the object level. The base is a marked closed hyperbolic genus-two surface with unit-speed geodesic flow and presentation

```text
Gamma=<a1,b1,a2,b2 | [a1,b1][a2,b2]=1>.
```

The cover tower is the pure homology tower `H_N=ker(Gamma -> H_1(Sigma;Z/NZ))`. It is not the residual inverse-limit object studied in the preceding branch, and a conclusion about one tower cannot repair the other. Owners are oriented primitive surface-group conjugacy classes; inverse classes remain separately oriented. For an owner with homology vector in `Z^4`, content `d` is the greatest common divisor of the absolute coordinates, with zero content treated as a separate case.

The normalization is immutable. Physical lifted time is multiplied by exactly `1/N`, and the logarithm of the raw lift-component product is multiplied by exactly `1/N^3`. Content-dependent changes, outcome-dependent weights, adaptive schedules, and favorable-panel selection are prohibited. The universal endpoint concerns all owner contents, not an average and not the content-one subproduct alone.

The revised research question is:

**Do the prospectively derived local factors for higher-content and zero-content owners already obstruct the frozen `1/N` and `1/N^3` full-owner recovery scheme; and only if those adverse tests are survived, what formal and analytic obligations remain for the content-one subproduct?**

The change is methodological. It does not assert that the candidate factors are correct or that an obstruction exists. It places the shortest discriminating theorem targets before the most expensive formal-topology and compact-uniform program. A higher- or zero-content obstruction would settle the universal endpoint negatively under the fixed scheme. Survival would justify continued work. A positive content-one statement, if eventually proved, would remain a restricted result.

The article is positioned as a closed-corpus theoretical research-program report. Its contribution is the review-adjudicated ordering of exact obligations: bind owners, derive adverse local factors, run falsification-first formal comparisons, and only then develop the contingent content-one branch. No novelty comparison was authorized, so no priority or originality claim is made.

# Evidence Boundaries for Ownerwise Renormalization in Pure Genus-Two Homology Covers

**Author:** Liang Wang  
**Affiliation:** School of Artificial Intelligence and Automation, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Luoyu Road 1037, 430070, Hubei, P.R. China  
**Email:** wangliang.f@gmail.com  
**Report date:** 2026-09-02 UTC  
**Research stage:** ARS Stage 1 Phase 4 composition  
**Report disposition:** `PHASE4_REPORT_DRAFT_READY_WITH_WARNINGS`

## Declarations

**Funding:** None.  
**Competing interests:** None declared.  
**Human-subjects status:** Not applicable. The proposed work is theoretical and exact computational mathematics and involves no human participants, personal data, animals, or interventions.  
**Data and execution status:** The report uses only the frozen Stage 1 literature and project-design corpus. No owner panel, cover calculation, coefficient comparison, tail estimate, numerical grid, limit, or canonical-result refresh is reported as executed.

## Abstract

P32 examines whether a fixed renormalization scheme can recover every base primitive-owner factor in a pure genus-two homology-cover tower. The candidate is restricted to `H_N=ker(Gamma -> H_1(Sigma;Z/NZ))`; it is distinct from, and cannot repair, the residual inverse-limit object studied earlier. The physical lifted period is to be scaled by exactly `1/N`, and the logarithm of the raw lift-component product by exactly `1/N^3`. A closed 26-source corpus was processed through bibliography construction, bounded source verification, a complete literature matrix, thematic synthesis, and an independent Devil's Advocate checkpoint. The evidence supports four ordered research packages: bind a complete oriented surface-group owner interface, prove ownerwise cover and lift algebra, construct the positive-content and zero-content formal comparisons self-containedly, and extract an absolute compact-uniform tail for every declared infinite limit order. No package is closed. In particular, the formal-precedent tension `CP-P32-004` remains unresolved, the exact owner factors remain derivation targets, and finite diagnostics cannot establish an infinite theorem. The report's contribution is a fail-closed separation of formal, analytic, and dynamical claims. Full-owner recovery and the secondary content-one analytic endpoint both remain unevaluated; arithmetic A0, automatic A2 credit, residual-tower rescue, and Route B remain unavailable.

**Keywords:** homology covers; primitive geodesics; ownerwise renormalization; formal power series; compact-uniform convergence; dynamical zeta functions

## 1. Introduction

Finite cover identities can look stronger than the objects they actually compare. A product may factor correctly at one modulus, a selected owner class may scale as intended, or a finite coefficient table may reproduce a known pattern. None of these observations alone establishes recovery of every primitive owner along a growing cover and owner schedule. P32 was designed to separate those levels before any global-product statement is allowed.

The candidate is the pure homology-cover tower of a marked closed hyperbolic genus-two surface. With

```text
Gamma=<a1,b1,a2,b2 | [a1,b1][a2,b2]=1>,
H_N=ker(Gamma -> H_1(Sigma;Z/NZ)),
```

the owner is an oriented primitive surface-group conjugacy class. Inversion remains separately oriented. The pure tower is nonresidual and is not the residual inverse-limit system from P27. This boundary is structural: a result for one tower cannot supply periodic owners to the other.

For an owner's homology vector, the project defines content `d` as the greatest common divisor of its four absolute coordinates. Positive content and zero content are treated separately. The proposed normalization is fixed in advance. Physical lifted time is multiplied by exactly `1/N`, and the raw lift-component log product is multiplied by exactly `1/N^3`. No content-dependent clock, exponent, owner weight, or post-outcome panel repair is permitted.

### Research question

**Does the paired frozen `1/N` clock and `1/N^3` logarithmic-normalization scheme recover the base primitive-owner factor for every owner under a certified target-blind exhaustion of the pure genus-two homology-cover calibrator?**

The universal full-owner endpoint is primary. A single certified higher-content or zero-content mismatch would obstruct it ownerwise. A content-one analytic subproduct is secondary and cannot erase that obstruction, substitute for the full primitive-owner product, or repair the residual tower. This report does not answer the scientific endpoint. It organizes the frozen evidence for the proof program and records where the evidence stops.

## 2. Literature and Theoretical Framework

### 2.1 Canonical owners, conjugacy, roots, and prefix completeness

The first source family concerns algorithmic group structure. Cannon (1984)<!--ref:P32-S01--><!--anchor:none:--> supplies finite combinatorial structure for cocompact discrete hyperbolic groups. Epstein and Holt (2006)<!--ref:P32-S02--><!--anchor:none:--> address terminating conjugacy in word-hyperbolic groups. Bridson and Howie (2005)<!--ref:P32-S03--><!--anchor:none:--> and Buckley and Holt (2013)<!--ref:P32-S04--><!--anchor:none:--> provide finite-subset and finite-list conjugacy interfaces. Lysenok (1990)<!--ref:P32-S05--><!--anchor:none:--> supplies the strongest verified root-extraction surface in the frozen corpus. Wang et al. (2025)<!--ref:P32-S06--><!--anchor:none:--> offer a 2025 surface-group normal-form, conjugacy, and root-finding candidate, but the source is a non-peer-reviewed preprint and uses a presentation not yet mapped to the frozen marked presentation.

Together, these sources support decomposing `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1` into several subcontracts: exact equality normal form, oriented conjugacy canonicalization, maximal primitive root, separate inverse handling, deterministic serialization, and certified prefix enumeration. They do not close the composite interface. Solving conjugacy for a supplied finite list is weaker than proving that a prefix contains every earlier eligible owner under the fixed ordering and has zero unresolved equality, conjugacy, and primitivity decisions.

### 2.2 Cover structure and homology-sensitive orbits

Jassim (1984)<!--ref:P32-S07--><!--anchor:none:--> and Sunada (1985)<!--ref:P32-S08--><!--anchor:none:--> supply finite abelian surface-cover and Riemannian-cover context. Phillips and Sarnak (1987)<!--ref:P32-S09--><!--anchor:none:-->, Katsuda and Sunada (1988)<!--ref:P32-S10--><!--anchor:none:-->, and Katsuda and Sunada (1990)<!--ref:P32-S11--><!--anchor:none:--> address geodesics or closed orbits refined by homology. This family makes deck order, splitting behavior, and homology-stratum abundance legitimate theorem interfaces. It does not derive P32's exact owner factor, prove that each lifted component is primitive, or choose the paired normalization. The project must prove those statements from the frozen deck action and owner content. Literature proximity cannot turn the choices `1/N` and `1/N^3` into validated consequences.

### 2.3 Primitive-orbit products and finite-cover analytic context

Selberg (1956)<!--ref:P32-S13--><!--anchor:none:--> supplies historical trace and zeta context, but its source-existence label remains `PLAUSIBLE` under the DOI-less authoritative record. Ruelle (1976)<!--ref:P32-S14--><!--anchor:none:--> provides primitive-orbit dynamical-zeta context. Parry and Pollicott (1983)<!--ref:P32-S15--><!--anchor:none:--> provide prime-orbit asymptotic context. Product theory, finite-cover factorization, and meromorphic continuation operate at a different level from P32's independent-owner coefficient comparison. None of these sources identifies the project formal variables with an infinite scalar product, proves coefficientwise recovery under the fixed normalization, or justifies passage through the infinite homology-cover schedule.

### 2.4 Counting and compact-uniform tails

Lalley (1989)<!--ref:P32-S19--><!--anchor:none:--> provides renewal and geodesic-counting methods. Margulis (1969)<!--ref:P32-S20--><!--anchor:none:--> supplies foundational prime-geodesic growth context. These works are candidates for an analytic-tail proof, not the proof itself. P32 requires an absolute bound on the exact logarithmic summand, uniform on every compact rectangle

```text
K(delta,T,R)={s: 1+delta<=Re(s)<=R, |Im(s)|<=T},
```

for every `delta>0`, finite `T>=0`, and finite `R>=1+delta`. The bound must also respect the owner strata and justify each iterated and diagonal limit order. An asymptotic title, an error term for a related counting function, or a finite numerical grid cannot be promoted into that conclusion.

### 2.5 Formal topology and the zero-content boundary

Neumann (1949)<!--ref:P32-S23--><!--anchor:none:--> supplies ordered-division-ring and well-ordered-support background. Snellman (1998)<!--ref:P32-S24--><!--anchor:none:--> supplies an inverse-limit, countably-many-variable topology precedent. Chiu et al. (2022)<!--ref:P32-S25--><!--anchor:none:--> provide adic-completion context in an unrelated geometric application. NIST DLMF Project (2026)<!--ref:P32-S26--><!--anchor:none:--> supplies elementary scalar power-series formulas and domain conditions.

All four sources are bounded to background roles. They expose why exponents, transition maps, completion, localization, and scalar specialization must be defined explicitly. They do not validate the project inverse-limit ring `R_+`, the separate nonnegative-rational Hahn object for `d=0`, the normalization, or any recovery endpoint. The Phase 3 pair `CP-P32-004`, which compares the Neumann and Snellman precedents, therefore remains `flagged_unresolved` with scholar confirmation pending.

## 4. Evidence-Synthesis Findings

### 4.1 The owner interface is a composite proof object

The first finding is that canonical owner enumeration cannot be delegated to an opaque normal-form call. A valid `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1` binding must prove the equality and oriented-conjugacy biconditionals in the exact marked presentation, return maximal primitive roots, canonicalize inverses separately, serialize owners deterministically, and certify that every requested prefix contains exactly the first eligible owners. An enumeration frontier without a completeness theorem is not enough.

The corpus supplies plausible components but no closed composite. Consequently, `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1=UNBOUND`, and every proposed owner panel remains not evaluated. No finite population may be padded, reordered, or repaired after outcomes.

### 4.2 Ownerwise lift algebra remains a derivation target

For positive content `d`, the Phase 1 program proposes to define `q_N=gcd(N,d)` and prove the deck order, primitive lift count, physical lift period, and normalized owner factor. Its target formulas include

```text
order_N(g)=N/q_N(g),
primitive lift count=N^3 q_N(g),
F_N,g(s)=(1-exp(-s ell(g)/q_N(g)))^(-q_N(g)).
```

These are proof obligations, not findings of the literature report. The project must also prove primitive-lift status. For `d=0`, it proposes a separate derivation with order one, lift count `N^4`, rescaled period `ell(g)/N`, normalized exponent `N`, and factor

```text
F_N,g^(0)(s)=(1-exp(-s ell(g)/N))^(-N).
```

The zero-content formula cannot be obtained by substituting `d=0` into the positive-content expression. No scientific value, mismatch coefficient, or scalar limit has been computed in this phase.

### 4.3 Formal recovery and analytic specialization are distinct endpoints

The proposed positive-content comparison uses independent owner variables and finite-support coefficient projections in a project-defined inverse-limit ring. A singleton-owner projection is intended to prevent a mismatch from canceling against other owners. Zero content uses a separately typed rational-exponent Hahn object. Because `CP-P32-004` is unresolved and every formal source is background-only, the report cannot assert that these objects are well constructed or that their localizations and transition maps behave as required.

Even a completed formal comparison would not automatically define an infinite scalar map. That map requires absolute convergence on the declared compact rectangles and independence from certified cofinal exhaustion. Formal equality, finite scalar evaluation, and infinite analytic convergence therefore remain separate gates.

### 4.4 Infinite schedules cannot be inferred from finite diagnostics

The theorem-level schedules are exactly

```text

m_k=2^k,
N'_k=2*(k!),
```

for every integer `k>=1`. The registered finite execution prefix is only `1<=k<=8`, and the fixed diagnostic panel sizes are `m in {8,16,32,64,128}`. Both finite diagnostic families remain `NOT_EXECUTED`. Even if executed later, they could check serialization or coefficients only. They could not establish convergence, cofinality, a diagonal theorem, or interchange of limits.

This distinction is a central evidence finding because several source clusters concern asymptotics or analytic continuation. Their presence does not shorten the universal quantifiers in the frozen design.

### 4.5 The four proof packages are ordered and fail-closed

The synthesis yields the following research architecture:

1. bind `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1` and its independent verifier;
2. prove the ownerwise cover and lift algebra, including the separate zero-content case;
3. construct and validate the formal owner-variable objects and coefficient projections; and
4. extract the exact absolute compact-uniform tail for every schedule and limit order.

Package one controls which owners can be named. Package two controls the factor being compared. Package three controls the meaning of formal equality and mismatch. Package four controls whether any infinite scalar specialization exists. None can substitute for another, and every package remains unexecuted.

### 4.6 Pure-tower conclusions cannot migrate to the residual object or to arithmetic A0

The evidence base concerns a generic marked hyperbolic surface and its pure homology covers. It provides no intrinsic map from rational primes to owners, no `log p` clock, and no arithmetic specificity. The calibrator therefore cannot supply A0. It could not relabel full-owner recovery, rescue P27's residual inverse-limit object, earn automatic positive arithmetic A2 credit, or open Route B.

## 5. Discussion

### 5.1 Interpretation

P32's main difficulty is not a shortage of adjacent theory. The corpus contains normal forms, conjugacy and root algorithms, cover structure, homology-refined orbit asymptotics, zeta and finite-cover factorization, continuation theory, error-term candidates, and formal-topology precedents. The difficulty is that the scientific endpoint crosses all of these interfaces while preserving exact owner coordinates and two fixed renormalizations.

The strongest counterargument is that a metadata- and abstract-level synthesis cannot establish the hypotheses needed for any package. That objection is decisive against a claim of feasibility or recovery. It does not defeat the actual contribution, which is the separation of obligations and stop states. The report makes it harder for a finite calculation, a favorable content class, or an imported formal analogy to be mistaken for the universal theorem.

### 5.2 Theoretical implications

The evidence architecture clarifies four distinctions. Canonical enumeration is stronger than decision on a supplied finite list. Cover-level factorization is different from equality of independent owner coordinates. Formal coefficientwise comparison is different from analytic scalar specialization. A restricted content-one endpoint is different from universal full-owner recovery.

These distinctions also explain why an obstruction could be informative. One exact higher-content or zero-content mismatch would refute the fixed full-owner recovery scheme without requiring a complete global product. Conversely, success on content one would remain secondary unless every other owner class and every formal gate were addressed.

### 5.3 Practical implications

The immediate research priority is interface binding, not numerical scale. A versioned `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1` contract should be tested against the frozen marked presentation and independently replayed before any panel request. The deck-order and primitive-lift proof should then be written ownerwise, with the zero-content case separated from the start. Only after the formal objects are self-contained should coefficient diagnostics be considered. Analytic tail extraction belongs last.

This order preserves interpretable failures. An unbound owner interface yields `PANEL_NOT_EVALUABLE`; insufficient population yields its own status; an exact owner mismatch yields `FULL_RECOVERY_OBSTRUCTED_OWNERWISE`; an absent tail yields a not-evaluable content-one analytic endpoint. These dispositions should not be collapsed into one binary success/failure label.

## 6. Limitations and Future Work

The literature report has several limitations. Claim-level locators are absent. The direct surface-group source is a non-peer-reviewed preprint whose presentation mapping remains unproved. The historical Selberg record is `PLAUSIBLE`, not `VERIFIED`. The Giulietti–Liverani–Pollicott source is correction-bound. The formal sources are background-only. General conflict-of-interest and retraction screens were not run. Most importantly, no source supplies the exact combined owner interface, formal algebra, or compact-uniform tail.

Future work should preserve the following sequence:

1. freeze the theorem, implementation, serialization, and test-vector binding for `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1`;
2. prove equality, oriented conjugacy, maximal roots, separate inverses, and prefix completeness in the exact presentation;
3. derive the positive-content and zero-content lift factors under the fixed `1/N` and `1/N^3` choices;
4. resolve `CP-P32-004` through a self-contained construction rather than a bibliographic analogy;
5. state the first valid singleton coefficient comparison before scalar length evaluation; and
6. extract a compact-uniform absolute tail and prove every iterated and diagonal limit order on the full schedules.

Finite diagnostics may be proposed only after the relevant proof packages close. Their role must remain certificate replay and stress testing, not evidence for an infinite theorem.

## 7. Conclusion and Bounded Recommendations

The closed evidence base supports a disciplined research program but no recovery theorem. General and surface-specific group algorithms do not yet form `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1`. Cover and homology literature does not validate the paired normalization. Product and continuation theory does not imply independent-owner equality. Counting results do not yet supply the exact compact-uniform tail. Formal precedents remain background, and `CP-P32-004` remains unresolved.

The recommended next package is therefore a proof-binding dossier for the owner interface and ownerwise lift algebra. It should precede any panel, coefficient table, or scalar grid. Full-owner recovery and content-one analytic convergence must stay separate. The pure tower must stay separate from the residual inverse-limit system. Under these boundaries, a proved obstruction, a not-evaluable interface, or eventual restricted positive result can each be reported without overstating its scope.

# P32 Stage 1 Phase 5 Editorial Review

## Input binding and review status

| Field | Bound value |
|---|---|
| Seat | `R10-P5-EIC` |
| Review role | Editor-in-Chief |
| Calibration | `NOT_CALIBRATED` |
| Phase-4 report SHA-256 | `b04d98c2bb6003b6a24d96fb005353f06b4b5ab5e776a21f1d3f5a4f9c9ed656` |
| Phase-4 claim-intent manifest SHA-256 | `8272166de965bb527874af8a3860cb3417f38aef81bed25099483a0e0203b732` |
| Phase-4 checkpoint SHA-256 | `4ed1635c3c8a8be4322583f526063f144a9b325aadec5e77ca3213f945d008f2` |
| New retrieval | `NOT_RUN` |
| Input modification | `NONE` |
| Overall verdict | `MAJOR_REVISION` |

## Overall assessment

The report is conceptually strong in separating four layers that are often conflated: canonical owner enumeration, ownerwise lift algebra, formal independent-owner coefficient comparison, and compact-uniform analytic specialization. The positive-content/zero-content split, the fixed `1/N` and `1/N^3` normalizations, and the refusal to infer an infinite theorem from finite schedules are all important safeguards.

The current draft is still an architecture for a theorem rather than a theorem or a complete formal-methods paper. The central owner factors are displayed only as derivation targets, the proposed formal rings and transitions are undefined and explicitly unresolved, the owner enumerator is unbound, and the compact-uniform limit statement is not written as a self-contained theorem with a proved tail. Originality and passage-level evidence are likewise unresolved. Major revision is therefore required before the work can be presented as an original mathematical contribution.

## Dimension judgments

| Dimension | Judgment | Evidence-based rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Originality and contribution | `NEEDS_REVISION` | The four-package decomposition and ownerwise separation may be useful, but the report performs no novelty assessment and does not establish whether the proposed formal comparison or normalization has precedent. |
| Methodological rigor | `NEEDS_REVISION` | The fixed object, schedules, and stop states are rigorous design choices. However, `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1`, the lift derivation, the formal topology, and the analytic tail are all unbound or unproved, so the scientific method is not executable. |
| Evidence sufficiency | `NEEDS_REVISION` | The 26-source corpus is broad and its correction/preprint limits are visible, but every citation is `anchor:none`, one foundational record is only `PLAUSIBLE`, and the formal sources are background-only. |
| Argument coherence | `STRONG` | The report consistently keeps pure and residual towers, positive and zero content, formal and analytic endpoints, and finite and infinite schedules separate. |
| Writing quality | `ADEQUATE` | The main distinctions are explained clearly, but undefined project symbols, dense status vocabulary, provenance comments, and the machine ledger require a publication-facing layer. |

## Concrete strengths

- The Introduction freezes the pure nonresidual homology-cover tower and explicitly prohibits migration of conclusions to the residual inverse-limit object.
- Sections 4.2 and 4.3 separate positive-content and zero-content factors and distinguish formal coefficient recovery from infinite scalar specialization.
- Section 4.4 states the full schedules and explicitly denies finite diagnostic prefixes any convergence or limit-interchange force.
- Section 4.5 orders four proof packages so that no panel can precede a certified owner interface and no scalar theorem can precede formal construction and an analytic tail.
- Section 4.6 maintains the absence of arithmetic A0 and prevents a restricted content-one result from becoming full-owner or Route evidence.

## Findings and required revisions

### Critical findings

None. The displayed formulas and schedules are consistently labeled as proposed targets or unexecuted diagnostics rather than proved results.

### Major findings

#### `P32-EIC-001` — The primary formal endpoint is not yet mathematically defined

**Exact section evidence:** Sections 2.5 and 4.3 refer to a project-defined inverse-limit ring `R_+`, localizations and projections, and a separate rational-exponent Hahn object; both sections state that `CP-P32-004` is unresolved and the constructions cannot yet be asserted to be well formed.

**Editorial consequence:** Without explicit rings, exponent monoids, transition maps, topology, localization conditions, and coefficient projections, “ownerwise recovery” has no stable formal truth condition.

**Required revision:** Give self-contained definitions and prove that all operations used by the comparison are well defined. Resolve the positive-content and zero-content objects separately and state exactly how finite-support singleton projections interact with the inverse system. Do not rely on analogy to the background sources.

#### `P32-EIC-002` — The central owner-factor formulas remain unproved targets

**Exact section evidence:** Section 4.2 displays `order_N(g)=N/q_N(g)`, a primitive lift count, the positive-content factor, and a separate zero-content factor, while repeatedly stating that these are proof obligations and that primitive-lift status is unproved.

**Editorial consequence:** These formulas generate the rest of the proposed comparison. Until their derivation and hypotheses are established, the normalization program cannot be assessed for correctness.

**Required revision:** Provide an ownerwise derivation from the deck action, including the deck order, component count, covering degree, primitivity of lifted components, scaled period, and logarithmic multiplicity. Treat `d=0` separately and state every condition under which the formulas hold.

#### `P32-EIC-003` — The universal owner quantifier has no certified enumeration interface

**Exact section evidence:** Sections 2.1 and 4.1 require equality, oriented conjugacy, maximal roots, separate inverses, deterministic serialization, and prefix completeness; the report concludes `SG2OwnerCanonical-v1=UNBOUND`.

**Editorial consequence:** The primary research question ranges over every primitive owner, but the draft cannot yet define or certify the sequence over which its exhaustion and singleton comparisons run.

**Required revision:** Bind the exact marked presentation to a complete canonical-owner theorem, serialization contract, and verifier. Prove the prefix-completeness invariant and distinguish it from decision on a supplied finite list before using any owner schedule in a theorem statement.

#### `P32-EIC-004` — The analytic endpoint is not a self-contained theorem

**Exact section evidence:** Sections 2.4 and 4.4 require an absolute logarithmic-summand bound uniform on every `K(delta,T,R)` and compatible with all iterated and diagonal schedules; Sections 6 and 7 state that no such exact tail has been extracted.

**Editorial consequence:** Listing relevant counting and continuation literature and fixed schedules does not establish convergence, cofinality, or exchange of limits.

**Required revision:** State the exact scalar functions, quantifier order, compact domain, summation order, limiting schedules, and desired equality. Then prove an absolute compact-uniform majorant and every limit passage used, or narrow the article to the formal finite-support endpoint.

#### `P32-EIC-005` — Evidence and contribution positioning remain incomplete

**Exact section evidence:** Section 3 records a bounded source pipeline; Section 6 acknowledges absent locators, a non-peer-reviewed surface-group candidate, a `PLAUSIBLE` Selberg record, correction-bound use, background-only formal sources, and no novelty assessment.

**Editorial consequence:** Neither the theorem transfers nor the originality of the proposed normalization/formal architecture can presently be evaluated.

**Required revision:** Provide the reproducible search and screening protocol, exact source passages and hypotheses for every imported component, and a separately authorized contribution comparison. Align the article type with the strongest result actually proved after revision.

### Minor findings

#### `P32-EIC-006` — Project-roadmap material competes with the mathematical narrative

**Exact section evidence:** Section 4.6, the conclusion, and the closed ledger repeatedly discuss P27 rescue, A0, A2, Route B, and project state.

**Editorial consequence:** These boundaries are important internally but distract from the pure homology-cover theorem program for external readers.

**Required revision:** Retain a concise scope paragraph in the article and move detailed cross-paper and Route bookkeeping to a linked project supplement.

#### `P32-EIC-007` — The AI verification disclosure is internally overbroad

**Exact section evidence:** The disclosure says all findings were verified against sources and then limits verification to metadata, abstracts, landing pages, corrections, and bounded upstream context.

**Editorial consequence:** The opening claim can be mistaken for full theorem-passage verification.

**Required revision:** Replace it with one accurate, bounded statement and preserve the `anchor:none` limitation in the publication metadata or supplement.

## Route-A and Route-B boundary

This editorial review grants no scientific Route status. P32 remains the pure genus-two homology-cover calibrator with arithmetic A0 unavailable, the formal Route-A tuple `UNASSIGNED`, positive arithmetic A2 absent, and Route B closed. Neither a future formal content-one result nor an editorial acceptance would repair the residual tower, establish full-owner recovery, or create Route credit.

## Procedural-independence and model disclosure

This review was produced by the `R10-P5-EIC` seat using the current Codex model family. The seat was procedurally separated from the Ethics, citation-integrity, and Devil's Advocate seats and did not inspect or synthesize their Phase-5 outputs. No external provider or cross-model transfer was authorized. Procedural separation does not imply statistically independent errors; the review is single-family and `NOT_CALIBRATED`.
